rationale: Both reviews converge on the same core technical issue (widening `== "cuda"` to `!= "cpu"` silently pulls in NPU/other accelerators, plus device_module resolved once at construction instead of per-encode) and both note the claimed test file/coverage doesn't exist in the tree — neither hits the ground truth's actual points (gcanlin's platform.device suggestion, the UT-removal exchange), so recall is low and roughly equal. X presents a 'confirmed empirically' terminal transcript for its fork_rng claim with the actual command elided as '...', which reads as fabricated proof rather than a real test, hurting its precision despite the underlying PyTorch claim being plausible; Y's findings are backed throughout by specific in-repo file:line quotes (including a real existing cuda/musa allowlist elsewhere in the codebase) that look like genuine grounded investigation. X is more actionable with ready-to-paste code diffs and clear Blocking/Should-fix/Nit triage, while Y's dense evidence-block format is thorough but harder to act on quickly. Neither has a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
